title: Incident-driven hotfix lifecycle for mixed-hosting rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: define and implement a clearly documented, testable hotfix lifecycle and automated orchestration primitives for model rollout regressions that can span Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for customer-facing regressions and provide predictable, auditable steps for: (1) triage and immediate mitigations, (2) rapid hotpatch + canary re-evaluation, (3) coordinated rollback or pinning per-tenant across environments, and (4) customer communications and post-incident follow-ups.

Key deliverables:
- A standard hotfix checklist with roles (SRE, Model Ops, Customer Success, PM) and explicit timeboxes for each step.
- An orchestration playbook that supports: tenant pinning, staged traffic remapping, timeboxed hotpatch windows, and fast rollback across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with automatic telemetry gating.
- Small automation: a CLI / API endpoint to trigger a cross-env rollback/pin operation with safeguards (RBAC, dry-run, pre-checks).
- Validation harness: automated smoke prompts + token-level latency/cost checks to run inside canaries before re-opening traffic.
- Communication templates for customer-facing and internal notifications and a postmortem template that includes model-eval diffs.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Playbook published in Confluence and reviewed by SRE, Model Ops, and Legal.
2) The CLI rollback endpoint can execute a tenant-level pin or global rollback in <= 10m for Hosted and Dedicated tests in staging. Private manual handshakes documented for air-gapped customers.
3) Smoke harness runs and returns pass/fail within configured timeout; pass gates traffic re-open.
4) Two oncall drills completed with <= 20% variance in execution time vs. timebox estimates.
5) Customer communication templates validated with Customer Success and used in one live escalation.

Out of scope for this ticket: full automation for every Private customer (those require account-specific runbooks) and large-scale multi-tenant reconfig that needs infra allocation changes. Those will be follow-ups.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Asha Patel: Created ticket after last week's P1 canary regression affecting embeddings latency for several hosted customers. Initial triage suggests kernel selection regression in runtime-1.19 that surfaced during low-latency optimization rollout. Need cross-team sync: SRE, Model Ops, CS.

2026-03-02 — Liam O'Connor: Ran canary replay in staging; reproduced elevated tail latency when KV cache hit ratio dropped under 0.6. Temporary mitigation: pinned affected tenants to model-v1.43. Filed PR for quick pin API (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4211).

2026-03-03 — Maya Chen (SRE): Added telemetry gating to canary flow: now the canary job fails fast if 95p latency > 1.5s or token cost increases > 12% (config in https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Canary+Gating).

2026-03-05 — Liam O'Connor: Drafted rollback CLI spec and dry-run semantics. Design note: dry-run returns proposed actions per environment and tenant list; must include residency-safe check for Private deployments. Spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yHotfixCLI-spec

2026-03-06 — Customer Success (Priya Rao): Coordinated initial customer comms for two affected tenants (Acct-328, Acct-441). Customers accepted temporary pinning; requested ETA on permanent fix. Logged as customer escalations: CS-2026-03-A.
progress_updates: 2026-03-07 — PoC rollback CLI implemented (alpha) that executes dry-run and a simulated apply for Hosted only. Tested with staging: tenant pin applied in ~6m. Next: add Dedicated execution path and audit logs.

2026-03-09 — Integrated smoke harness into canary pipeline: executes three golden prompts and checks token-level delta + semantic similarity. Two failures observed for quantized kernel path; blocking canary reopen until hotpatch validated.
2026-03-10 — PR opened for audit log schema and RBAC checks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4239 — awaiting security review.
2026-03-11 — Oncall drill scheduled for 2026-03-14 to run through hotfix checklist end-to-end with simulated Private customer communication workflow. Objective: validate timeboxes and handoff docs.
postmortem_strategy: When a regression reaches customer-impacting status: (1) immediate triage note and assign hotfix lead, (2) collect golden prompts and telemetry diff, (3) decide hotpatch vs. rollback within 30 minutes, (4) if hotpatch chosen, limit to a timeboxed canary with gating and explicit rollback trigger, (5) if rollback chosen, execute CLI with audit and notify CS and account owners. Post-incident: run a model-eval regression check against the release candidate and schedule a write-up that includes token-cost delta and perf profile changes.
followups: Implement Dedicated execution path and audit-safe apply for the rollback CLI
Formalize Private/air-gapped checklist + customer-specific runbook template
Add automated tenant-priority queueing to the rollback CLI (so paying accounts can be prioritized)
Ingest canary gating results into Console dashboard widget for oncall visibility
